name: Clabber
description: Clabber is a trick-taking card game of the Jass/Belote family, uniquely popular in Evansville, Indiana and surrounding areas. It is played with a 24-card deck (Ac-9) and features complex trump rankings and a 'meld' system where card combinations like 'Dad' (3-card sequence) and 'Mule' (4 Jacks) score bonus points. The game is highly strategic, requiring players to choose trumps carefully and compete for the prestigious 'last trick' bonus. It is colloquially known as 'Dad' after its most common sequence meld.

content.text: Clabber is a trick-taking card game of the Jass/Belote family, uniquely popular in Evansville, Indiana and surrounding areas. It is played with a 24-card deck (Ac-9) and features complex trump rankings and a 'meld' system where card combinations like 'Dad' (3-card sequence) and 'Mule' (4 Jacks) score bonus points. The game is highly strategic, requiring players to choose trumps carefully and compete for the prestigious 'last trick' bonus. It is colloquially known as 'Dad' after its most common sequence meld.

Brought to Indiana by German and Central European immigrants, Clabber is a local evolution of the European Klabberjass. It became a cultural staple in Evansville, often played in taverns and social clubs.
4 players in fixed partnerships (North-South vs East-West).
24 cards and a 'Clabber' score sheet (typically with 4 columns for tracking team scores and addition-checks).
Dealer deals all 24 cards one at a time clockwise; each player receives six cards. The last card (dealer's) is turned face up; its suit is the trump candidate for the first round of bidding.

items.text: Two-Player Clabber: Players receive 9 cards each (6 initially, then 3 after bidding). A 'dead hand' of 6 cards remains out of play.
Three-Player Clabber: Each player is dealt 8 cards. The trump maker must beat both opponents individually.
Wadesville 300-point sequence: In some regions, a 6-card sequence is recognized as a '300-point' meld.
